approved: Universities Accord (Opening the Doors of Opportunity) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill overhauls how the government pays for university places, steering funds toward students who have historically missed out on higher education.

The Australian Tertiary Education Commission would hand out Commonwealth-supported places to universities using a new managed-growth pot, and extra needs-based grants would go to institutions enrolling disadvantaged learners.
The bill backs this with $2.5 billion in new government money and is expected to add 200,000 first-year domestic students over the next ten years.
The bill creates a Managed Growth Funding System for Commonwealth-supported places.
It sets up Needs-based Funding grants for universities that enroll students from poorer families, Indigenous students, and those at regional campuses.
It gives the Australian Tertiary Education Commission the job of allocating those places and international student places when the minister decides.
It lets the minister set rules for how international student places are handed out.
It changes information-sharing laws so the commission can get data from the Ombudsman and the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency.

Universities and higher education providers, along with students from low-income, Indigenous, and regional or remote backgrounds, plus international students when the government manages their numbers.

Supported the Universities Accord (Opening the Doors of Opportunity) Bill 2026, describing his mother's path from a lighthouse keeper's daughter to university graduate, and detailed the bill's new managed-growth funding system, needs-based equity payments of over $1,500 per disadvantaged student, and $3.6 billion in additional higher education investment expected to create 230,000 more commencing domestic university places over the next decade.

Introducing the Universities Accord (Opening the Doors of Opportunity) Bill 2026, the seventh piece of legislation implementing the Australian Universities Accord, the speaker said it will deliver around 16,000 additional fully funded Commonwealth supported university places from 2027, rising to 19,000 by 2030, adding roughly 230,000 commencing students over the next decade. She said the bill embeds needs-based funding for disadvantaged, First Nations and regional students and represents an additional $3.6 billion in university funding over ten years, and the bill passed its second reading.
